results.text:
Open Targets association scores with acute myeloid leukemia (EFO_0000222), for the five genes with the lowest adjusted p-values in your run:

| Rank | Gene | padj | log2FC | AML association score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ISG15 | 1.00e-38 | 4.00 | 0.437 |
| 2 | MX1 | 1.12e-38 | 3.55 | 0.122 |
| 3 | IFIT1 | 1.25e-38 | 3.10 | 0.385 |
| 4 | OAS1 | 1.40e-38 | 2.21 | 0.051 |
| 5 | RSAD2 | 1.57e-38 | 2.58 | 0.268 |

I ranked the genes by sorting `de_results.csv` on `padj`. Scores are on a 0–1 scale.

- **The ranking is nearly tied.** The top 5 padj values span only 1.0e-38 to 1.57e-38, and genes ranked 6 and later (LOC105035 and others) continue at almost the same level. Those padj values are implausibly small for n=3 per group. Treat the order as arbitrary, and check how the table was computed before you rely on the rank. This is a statistical concern about the run, not something I have verified.
- **The scores are weak to moderate.** Even ISG15, the highest, scores 0.437. These are interferon-stimulated genes, so the scores reflect general evidence linking them to leukemia. They do not show that your treatment acts through AML-relevant biology.
- **Your samples are not AML.** The association scores come from curated genetic, literature, and other evidence in Open Targets. They are not a test of your data.
- **Each gene returned only two disease associations**, AML and "neoplasm". I took the AML score from that list.

I can also check the next-ranked genes. Or I can look at AML scores for the upregulated interferon genes as a set, rather than only the top five by p-value.

plan.analytical_narrative: No dataset facts were available at planning time (the profile was not ready), so this plan makes no assumptions about assay, organism, conditions or replication. steps.name: QC and differential expression
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the conditions in the sample metadata, and how large and how reliable are the effects?
steps.description: Inspect the input expression matrix and sample metadata to establish the data type (raw counts vs normalized values vs microarray), organism, the condition factor(s), replicate numbers, and any batch or other covariates. Run sample-level QC (library size/ distribution, low-expression filtering, PCA/sample correlation, outlier check). Fit the appropriate model with the condition as the factor of interest and adjust for identified batch covariates when they are not confounded with condition. Report all pairwise contrasts when there are more than two conditions. Output full results tables (log2 fold change, p-value, adjusted p-value) per contrast, a significant-gene table, and volcano and PCA plots. Gene annotation (symbols) may use the GENCODE annotation if the IDs are Ensembl IDs and the organism is human.
steps.context: Dataset specifics were not available when this plan was written. The agent must confirm the facts from the files themselves and state them in its summary. I submitted a two-step plan, and the harness accepted it. I couldn't read the data profile or the workspace files (those tools returned "not available"). So the plan names no organism, conditions, assay or sample counts. I didn't run any analysis or check the packages against the package list.

plan.title: Treated vs control DE + hallmark/KEGG enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: Human bulk RNA-seq, 58,302 genes x 6 samples (treated T1-T3 vs control C1-C3), raw gene-level counts, with a sample sheet that carries a batch column. DE runs on raw counts with DESeq2 (Wald test, BH FDR 0.05, apeglm shrinkage). Sample C3 has a library size 40% below the median. Median-of-ratios size factors handle depth differences, but the QC step checks C3 on PCA and sample distances before deciding whether to keep it. C3 stays by default, and a sensitivity run without it is reported. With n=3 per group, an exclusion would leave n=2 in the control group. The batch column was not readable at planning time, so the step must tabulate batch against group. It adds batch to the design only if every batch level is not confounded with group. If batch coincides with group, it fits group alone and flags that batch cannot be separated from treatment. Enrichment is a second step because it needs the full ranked DE table. It runs fgsea on all tested genes ranked by the Wald statistic against hallmark and KEGG MEDICUS gene sets, and it needs symbols from the GENCODE v46 annotation. The knowledge service was unavailable, so the steps are ungrounded; the draft passed the rule check with no findings. The input files could not be opened during planning, so the file formats and the batch layout are unverified.

steps.name: QC, annotation and DESeq2 differential expression
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (T1-T3) and control (C1-C3) in human bulk RNA-seq, and is the low-depth sample C3 or the batch column a problem?
steps.description: Load the raw count matrix (58,302 genes x 6) and the sample sheet (sample, group, batch). Check that the column names match the sample IDs. Map gene identifiers to gene symbols with a human gene annotation (GENCODE v46 GTF from the reference store). Report how many identifiers fail to map and how duplicate symbols are resolved. Do QC: library sizes, log-transformed (VST) PCA and sample-distance heatmap, and an explicit assessment of C3 (library size 40% below the median). Tabulate batch against group. If batch levels are not confounded with group, include batch in the design (~ batch + group). Otherwise use ~ group and flag the confounding. Filter low-count genes with edgeR filterByExpr (group-aware). Run DESeq2 with a Wald test for treated vs control (control as reference) and BH FDR alpha 0.05. Apply apeglm log2FC shrinkage for effect sizes. Write the full results table, with the unshrunken Wald statistic for every tested gene, a filtered significant-gene table, a PCA plot, a volcano plot and a heatmap of the top DE genes. Run a sensitivity analysis without C3 and report the overlap of significant genes with the main run.

The number of significant genes at padj<0.05 is reported, with the up and down split
The decision on C3 is documented, with the without-C3 sensitivity overlap
The batch vs group cross-tabulation and the final design formula are stated
The p-value histogram is checked for sanity
Annotation mapping rate is reported

Control must be the reference level
Do not drop C3 from the primary analysis unless QC shows it to be a clear outlier by clustering, and then state this
Do not fit batch if it coincides with group
caveats: n=3 per group gives limited power and unstable dispersion estimates
The filter-based thresholds are the defaults of filterByExpr and not tuned

The plan was accepted. It has two steps. I could not open the count matrix or the sample sheet, so none of it has been run against your data.

**Step 1: QC, differential expression and onset dose (DESeq2).**
- **QC and batch:** The step runs QC and tabulates batch against dose. It adds batch to the model only if batch is not confounded with dose. The sample sheet was unreadable here, so this is unchecked.
- **Dose-responsive genes:** A likelihood-ratio test across the four dose levels finds them, at FDR below 0.05.
- **Per-dose contrasts:** Wald contrasts of 1, 10 and 100 nM against 0 nM use apeglm-shrunken log fold changes.
- **Onset dose:** This is the lowest tested dose that is significant against 0 nM, with a minimum shrunken fold-change of 0.5. Each responder is also labelled monotonic up, monotonic down or non-monotonic.
- **Unresolved genes:** Genes that pass the overall test but no single dose are labelled "unresolved onset".
- **Sensitivity check:** A trend test on log-dose is run alongside.

**Step 2: hallmark enrichment (fgsea).** It runs fgsea on the human hallmark gene sets for each dose contrast. It also runs an over-representation test on each onset class. This step depends on step 1.

**Limits and assumptions:**
- Onset can only be resolved to 1, 10 or 100 nM. With three replicates per dose, low-dose responses will often be missed, so onsets will tend to look later than they are.
- The count rows are probably Ensembl IDs. Step 1 maps them to gene symbols using the GENCODE v46 annotation in the reference store. If the mapping fails, the enrichment step cannot run on symbols.
- I left out benchmark-dose and point-of-departure modelling. There are only four dose levels, no benchmark-dose package is installed, and your question asks for onset, not a benchmark dose.
